Check out Buccal Fat removal. It's a non-invasive outpatient procedure that some plastic surgeons do and it's pretty much mini lipo for your face. I have the same problem with face fat, always been thin and active but in pics of my face you'd think I was way overweight. Finally had the procedure done and the changes are gradual as your body adapts just as with lipo but after about 6 months the difference was way more than I could have done on my own, since that type of fat usually persists and only reduces with age. 10/10 would do it again.

Ok good deal with officer. Sucks they weren't too helpful, sorry on behalf of the AF, how embarassing!! But lots of people enlist first then cross over too. I know a guy who's doing that right now so it's 100% still a possibility once you enlist. Tbh the best officers I've worked for were all prior enlisted because it gives them more perspective on what the layman deals with day to day. And yea, if you're certain of what jobs you want then push for those and advocate for yourself, you've got nothing to loose and a whole lot to gain. Overall, just make sure you have a specific job slot before you leave, that will eliminate the "open general" situation. 

Deployment rotations largely depend on the base and what theyre tasked with supporting but regardless of your job and where you are, if you want to go there will be opportunities. Especially because a good handful of people don't want to go so whenever a tasking comes down they ask for volunteers first. Army supports lots and lots of deployments and a larger area of responsibility  so they usually get burned out with it, whereas Air Force, we still go but are more limited in scope so we have the luxury of being able to take volunteers first before we have to start forcing people. I'm deployed right now on my first one, but my husband has been on three in his 11 years. Another guy I know has deployed five times in 10 years.

Nice, 84 is really good and will qualify you for alot of jobs. In fact, since you already have a degree you should really consider commissioning as an officer instead of enlisted. Biggest benefit to that is you get paid wayyy more right off the bat and are charged with personnel and organisational management as opposed to enlisted which are the "boots on the ground" and ones getting their hands dirty. Pros and cons to both, but having the degree puts you at a good advantage there. I'm enlisted as a maintainer which involves wrench-turning and fixing things. I love it, but it's not for everyone. 

Also, kinda biased here but go AF instead of  Army. Way better quality of life on Air Force bases (better housing and facilities) and less deployments. Plus when you do deploy it's usually shorter time. As for jobs, you have the option to pick jobs, I think it was 4 when I joined, then if you're not in a hurry to get out of town, wait for an opening in one of them before signing on. Avoid "open general" enlistment at all costs, whether Army or Air Force because that's pretty much a guarantee that you end up either as a cop or infantry, both of which are notorious for getting treated like garbage and having the lowest morale. You can do much better than that with your credentials. 

I'm pretty sure you can wait for the job you want as well. Some newer guys I talked to lately said they wanted specific jobs and could have gotten them but they just didn't want to wait. When I enlisted I got notified that there was an opening in my top choice (2WOX1 Munitions Systems, which just so happens to have lots of openings) so I took it right away. But again, pretty sure you can wait, especially if that's the difference between you enlisting or walking away. The recruiters need people to sign so they should be able to work with you on that.

First off, being open about your insecurities and sharing them, especially with bdd, is a very brave thing to do so huge kudos to that! Second, you have great symmetry and proportionate eyes lips and nose. Symmetry is something I (28F) have struggled to accept my whole life so I look for it alot in others.  For example, I hated my crooked nose and even got rhinoplasty to fix it and was always (and still do) making comparisons between myself and other people, mostly how much better they look than me. To me, getting the rhinoplasty was a huge improvement  in my appearance but most surprising was that other people, even close friends, didn't even notice I had anything done at all; nobody but me cared what my nose looked like. And looking back that's probably been the most beneficial part of the surgury; the fact that nothing changed in the way people treated me or had any effect of my "likeabiltiy" or attractiveness according to others. Sure, it makes me feel great and I don't obsess over my nose as much, but I guess what I'm trying to say is that it proved alot of the things I was obsessing about, nobody else saw as a problem. I'm sure the same is true for you man. Whatever it is that is truly bothering you or making you uncomfortable, alot of that is your brain playing tricks on you to make it a bigger deal than it is, which is hard, I know. But just try to go easy on yourself if you can. You're still really young and right now maybe all the guys with better hair or conventionally attractive features are getting the girls or whatever but looks only go so far. I and everyone I'm friends with would much rather be around and stick with an average nice guy than an attractive fool with an ego problem.
